agree.reason: A reader who is happy saving $25 a visit gets a one-time $99 discount and a vague insurance point, which gives little reason to pay more on every visit after that, so most readers like this one would not book.

honest.reason: It doesn't promise the same cleaner every time, but it tells each reader 'you told us two things' when the exit surveys only give overall results, and this reader never complained about cleaners; 'we've fixed it' also claims more than a few months of results can show.

works_the_facts.reason: It works out none of the useful figures: not the $25 gap, not what the $99 first visit saves, and not that only 1 of 18 cleaners has left since July compared with 7 the year before.

right_comparison.reason: It admits the app services cost less and says they use contractors, but never says their visits are uninsured, so the insurance point doesn't set the two apart, and it gives no sign of the trend in cleaner turnover.

qualification.reason: The backup cleaner for sick days is a fair hedge, but the $99 offer has no December 31 deadline and the email gives no way to check that cleaners now stay.

objections.reason: It deals with price only partly and leaves out no-contract and cancel-any-time, which would lower the risk of trying, while it spends space on a cleaner-turnover complaint this reader never made.

fit.reason: It is an email of about 150 words as asked, but it leaves placeholders for the company and owner names that the writer knew, and it has no reply-to-book option or phone number.
